content.value_statement: Teams lose time when code style, validation, and workflow decisions vary across files. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code consistent standards to apply during development.
actual_capabilities: Applies naming, formatting, and structure guidance across common programming languages.
Guides comment and docstring decisions with focus on useful context.
Recommends error handling patterns for user messages, logging, retries, and cleanup.
Promotes client-side and server-side validation with sanitization guidance.
Helps keep dependencies, frameworks, file structure, and workflows consistent.
limitations: It provides standards guidance, not automated linting or formatting by itself.
It does not replace project-specific rules stored outside the skill files.
It cannot verify behavior without access to the target codebase and tests.
It gives general guidance that may need adaptation for regulated environments.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check whether code changes follow naming, comments, validation, and error handling conventions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Choose patterns for files, dependencies, validation, and error handling before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Create Team Standards
use_cases.description: Use the reference files as a baseline for shared coding and workflow conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small code change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change against the global standards. Focus on names, formatting, comments, and avoidable duplication.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for service or API code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global standards to improve error handling. Check user messages, logging, cleanup, retries, and propagation boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Feature Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this feature plan against global standards. Cover validation, security boundaries, file structure, dependencies, and framework consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Project Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for global standards alignment. Identify convention gaps, repeated patterns, dependency concerns, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a new API endpoint with minimal validation.
output: Validation should run on both the request boundary and any domain service boundary.
Error messages should be clear for users and should avoid leaking internal details.
The endpoint should follow the existing route and file naming patterns.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to add a new package for date parsing.
output: First check whether the project already has a date utility or approved dependency.
Document the reason for a new package if existing tools do not meet the requirement.
Add tests for edge cases such as invalid dates and timezone boundaries.

output_examples.input: A team needs shared rules for comments and documentation.
output: Comments should explain intent, tradeoffs, and non-obvious behavior.
Remove comments that repeat clear code behavior or have become outdated.
Public interfaces should include concise documentation for parameters and results.

best_practices: Load the relevant reference file before making detailed standards decisions.
Compare new code with nearby project patterns before adding new abstractions.
Run project tests and quality checks after applying standards changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a substitute for project-specific requirements.
Do not add new dependencies before checking existing tools and conventions.
Do not apply generic standards when local code has a clear established pattern.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply consistent coding style, comments, validation, error handling, dependencies, and project workflow conventions.

faq.question: Does it run formatters or linters?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but the agent can still use project tools when available.

faq.question: Can it support different programming languages?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is language-neutral and references common patterns across frontend, backend, and infrastructure code.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify standards issues in naming, structure, comments, validation, and error handling.

faq.question: Does it handle security concerns?
faq.answer: It includes validation, sanitization, dependency, and secret-handling guidance, but it is not a full security scanner.

faq.question: How should teams customize the guidance?
faq.answer: Teams should add project-specific rules and keep the reference files aligned with their actual codebase.
